name: Perihelion Scar

detectability.signature: Localized temporal dilation field with zero entropy flux and anomalous tachyon reflection

proximity: Chronometers begin to drift, losing synchronization with external reference clocks
Light from within the field appears subtly blue-shifted at the boundary edges
contact: Complete temporal arrest — objects and organisms freeze at the moment of entry
Communication signals entering the field do not return or propagate further
Ship systems halt mid-cycle with no degradation or power loss
prolonged_exposure: Permanent temporal displacement upon extraction — subjects may emerge seconds or centuries out of sync
Molecular bonds locked in stasis resist manipulation for hours after removal
Psychological trauma from perceived instantaneous transition across elapsed external time

age: At least 4,000 years based on the oldest frozen vessels identified within
phenomena: A fleet of warships from the Sethári Dominion hangs motionless inside the field, weapons mid-fire, frozen in the final moments of a battle that never ended
Energy beams and projectiles are suspended between ships, casting permanent threads of light through the frozen tableau
The boundary shimmers faintly, and objects thrown into it stop instantly with no deceleration — momentum simply ceases
hazards: Any vessel or crew entering the field becomes trapped in temporal stasis with no known method of extraction
The irregular boundary shifts by meters over decades, potentially engulfing nearby stationary objects
Temporal disorientation affects crews operating near the boundary for extended periods
opportunities: The frozen fleet contains intact examples of Sethári Dominion technology, lost to history for millennia
Study of the boundary mechanics could yield breakthroughs in temporal manipulation and preservation science
The battle formation reveals tactical doctrines and force compositions of a civilization otherwise known only through ruins
known_incidents: Salvage operator Dren Kosvari lost both arms to the boundary in 2203 when the field edge shifted during an attempted probe retrieval — the arms remain visible, frozen in place, centimeters beyond the threshold
description: Perihelion Scar is a volume of space where time has stopped. Within its irregular boundary, a fleet of ancient warships hangs in perfect stillness, caught in the fury of a battle that will never conclude. Weapons fire links the vessels in frozen threads of light, and the hulls show damage arrested mid-rupture — metal peeled back, atmosphere crystallized in the act of venting. The scene is illuminated by weapons that have been firing for four thousand years without advancing a single photon further.

The stasis field is absolute. Nothing that enters moves again, and nothing inside degrades, decays, or changes state. Probes sent across the boundary halt instantly, their telemetry cutting off mid-transmission. The effect extends uniformly through the irregular volume, and the boundary itself is sharp enough to bisect objects at the atomic level. Chronometric instruments within two hundred kilometers become unreliable, and crews report a persistent unease — a sense of standing beside something that has divorced itself from the flow of the universe.

The frozen fleet belongs to the Sethári Dominion, a spacefaring civilization that collapsed approximately four millennia ago. Historical records are fragmentary, but the ship configurations suggest this was a major engagement — possibly the battle that ended the Dominion itself. How the stasis field formed is unknown. Some theorists propose a temporal weapon misfired; others believe the field is natural and the fleet was simply unlucky. The Sethári left no records of encountering anything similar, which lends weight to the weapon hypothesis.

Perihelion Scar draws a steady stream of researchers, historians, and treasure hunters, all circling the boundary and peering at technology they cannot touch. Several academic institutions maintain long-term observation posts, cataloging the frozen ships through high-resolution imaging. Proposals to breach the field surface periodically, each more ambitious and less funded than the last. For now, the battle endures — a silent monument to a war that time itself refuses to let finish.
